text: In Monaco, locals are banned from their own casino.
Monaco is just two square kilometers, smaller than New York's Central Park.
About 39,000 people live here, but fewer than one in four are actually citizens.
Many moved in for one big reason.
And the famous Monte Carlo casino?
Citizens can't gamble in its gaming rooms.
It was built in the 1860s to save Monaco from going broke, with tourists' money, not locals.
I live here, and I can't even play?
Monaco is also running out of room, so it builds new land in the sea.
Six hectares, worth about a billion euros.
And its whole coastline, under four kilometers.
